newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola in marketing deal with CBS.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola in marketing deal with CBS.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co and Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS television network said Tuesday they have a $50 million deal giving the beverage giant exclusive advertising rights on a variety of programs.
Coca-Cola will be the exclusive soft-drink sponsor of the 1998 Olympic Winter games, "The Late Show with David Letterman," the Grammy Awards, the Country Music Awards and other programming.
Different brands of Coca-Cola products will be matched to specific programs. The company said those decisions will be based on demographics and the "personality" of each brand.

"This investment not only allows us to link our brands all year long with programs and promotions that effectively reach our customers, but these CBS properties truly reflect the broad appeal and specialness with which we want our brands associated," Coca-Cola Vice President Chuck Fruit said in a statement.
The programs on which Coca-Cola will advertise through the agreement reach an audience in the 25 to 54 age bracket, a CBS spokesman said.
The agreement is in force from October 1997 to September 1998.
